text:
Savigny's Volksgeist holds that law is not invented by legislators but grows organically from a people's customs, culture and shared consciousness. Both "Law develops gradually out of a people's customs and shared consciousness" and "A society's law is a reflection of its culture" follow directly from that idea. So the statement least likely to follow is any claim that law should be a universal, rational code imposed from above regardless of a people's history. I can't see your actual options, so I can't pick the exact one.
